Practice · An 85-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 28%), moderate Alzheimer dementia, and creatinine clearance of 32 mL/min has improved after intravenous furosemide for fluid overload. Her regular medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 102/58 mm Hg. Her family asks about sacubitril/valsartan. The team is assessing tolerability and whether to switch. If an ACE-inhibitor-to-ARNI switch is selected, which initiation plan follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with heart failure (EF 35%), permanent atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes is admitted with volume overload. She functions independently, but her daughter reports recent difficulty managing medications. Her medications are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, renal-adjusted apixaban, and metformin already withheld during acute illness. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), and BNP 1850. ECG shows atrial fibrillation at 78 beats/min with QRS 118 ms. Which approach to spironolactone follows Hazzard's safety guidance?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost about 7 kg in four months. He takes small bites, chews extensively, reports food going 'the wrong way,' and has a wet, gurgly voice after meals. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily; creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. Modified barium swallow shows vallecular residue and delayed swallow initiation. Which statement correctly characterizes rehabilitative swallowing therapy considered after this assessment?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has worsening burning foot pain for three months. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin; HbA1c is 8.2%, and monofilament sensation is absent bilaterally. He lives alone and recently stopped driving because of pain. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily caused severe dizziness. Which listed analgesic option belongs to the serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor class?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment has recurrent falls, reduced activity, and increasing need for help with finances and medications. Examination shows bradykinesia, reduced arm swing, and a positive pull test. He takes metformin and lisinopril. Which assessment specifically investigates a possible blood-pressure or medication contribution to the falls?
Practice · An older man with hypertension and a previous myocardial infarction is being considered for a beta-blocker. Which consideration supports its use according to Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis has recurrent pain rated 7/10 that limits shopping. A course of three hyaluronic acid injections six months ago initially helped. She has heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and stage 3b CKD, and takes furosemide, lisinopril, and carvedilol. Examination shows an effusion and crepitus. She is reluctant to undergo the knee replacement recommended by her surgeon. Which intra-articular option has the strongest guideline support for short-term relief of her knee pain?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with CLL takes ibrutinib 420 mg/day. He also has hypertension treated with lisinopril 10 mg and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 45); he takes aspirin 81 mg. He presents with three weeks of progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea and five days of dark stools. He is pale, with BP 128/78, heart rate 96, no orthostatic changes, and no lymphadenopathy. Hemoglobin is 6.8 g/dL (baseline 11.2), MCV 82, platelets 165,000, WBC 42,000 with 85% lymphocytes, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.4). He has received one unit of packed red cells and is hemodynamically stable. Which statement about ibrutinib is relevant to reviewing his bleeding risk?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with HFpEF (EF 58%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and biopsy-proven transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis has NYHA class II symptoms despite furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Echocardiography shows LV wall thickening and grade 2 diastolic dysfunction. Which treatment is the TTR stabilizer described in Hazzard as reducing mortality versus placebo in ATTR-ACT?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is being assessed for home palliative care after three admissions in four months for heart-failure exacerbations. She has ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 25%), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24 mL/min/1.73 m²), and mild cognitive impairment. She takes furosemide 80 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and spironolactone 12.5 mg daily. She lives with her daughter, who works full time. The patient says she wants “no more hospitals,” but her daughter insists on calling emergency services whenever she becomes breathless. What should be done next to address their differing care expectations?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with hypertension and mild frailty walks with a walker and covers 5.2 meters in 8 seconds. Her baseline blood pressure is 148/82 on amlodipine 5 mg daily. In a trial she is assigned to an intensive systolic blood pressure target below 120 mm Hg. After amlodipine titration and addition of lisinopril, her blood pressure is 118/68 seated and 114/66 standing. She feels well and reports more energy. Which interpretation of the SPRINT evidence supports continuing her tolerated regimen with monitoring?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 22) presents after 3 days of productive cough, fever and delirium. He has fallen twice that day and missed medications. His usual drugs are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Temperature is 38.8°C, BP 95/60 mmHg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Chest radiography shows right lower-lobe consolidation; WBC is 16.2, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.2) and glucose 340 mg/dL. Oxygenation and hemodynamic support are being addressed. Which infection-directed strategy accords with Hazzard while microbiology results are pending?

Practice · A 75-year-old man with hypertension, prediabetes, and BPH takes chlorthalidone 25 mg daily and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. His blood pressure is 146/84. He reports dizziness on standing quickly and nocturia four to five times nightly that disrupts sleep. Glucose is 118, potassium 3.4, and creatinine 1.1. When reviewing possible thiazide adverse effects, which strategy follows the principles described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 73-year-old woman hospitalized with a heart failure exacerbation receives intravenous furosemide 40 mg twice daily. She has had no bowel movement since admission four days ago. Her home polyethylene glycol 17 g daily was omitted. She also takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and spironolactone and eats regular meals. Potassium is 3.8, magnesium 1.9, and creatinine 1.2. Which description correctly explains the action of polyethylene glycol if it is restarted?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with severe osteoarthritis and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38) has inadequate relief from acetaminophen 1 g three times daily. She has hypertension and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 45%, and takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. If an opioid trial is warranted after other treatments have been reviewed, which agent does Hazzard place before other opioids?

Practice · A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) receives home-based primary care. Her daughter found her unconscious twice in the past month, both times early in the morning before breakfast. She takes glimepiride 4 mg once daily with breakfast, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Her latest HbA1c is 6.8%, creatinine clearance is 58 mL/min, and prebreakfast fingerstick glucose readings range from 68 to 95 mg/dL. Which approach to the sulfonylurea agrees with Hazzard when hypoglycemia is a concern?
Practice · A 78-year-old man with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction takes a low-dose ACE inhibitor. He is to switch to sacubitril/valsartan. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · A 72-year-old man reports worsening urinary frequency, nocturia four to five times nightly, and a weak stream for six months. His AUASI is 18. He has hypertension, diabetes, and recent falls, takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, and lives alone. Which drug treats BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms through selective alpha-1A blockade?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes, osteoarthritis, and newly diagnosed mild cognitive impairment takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, celecoxib 200 mg daily, and acetaminophen 500 mg four times daily. She develops ankle edema, an eight-pound weight gain over two weeks, and worsening knee pain. Blood pressure is 165/95 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, and creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 1.4 mg/dL. Which change directly removes an NSAID exposure while retaining a non-NSAID analgesic strategy?
Practice · Hyperkalemia develops after spironolactone is added to lisinopril in an older man with CKD. Which renal action of spironolactone contributes?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?
Practice · Why must sacubitril/valsartan (ARNi) initiation be timed carefully relative to a prior ACE inhibitor?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?
Practice · A woman treated for hypertension develops hyponatremia and hypokalemia. Which drug class is linked to this pattern in Hazzard’s table of antihypertensive medications for older adults?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman presents after a fall and reports a month of dizziness on standing. She takes amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg each morning. Blood pressure is 138/78 supine and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 68 to 74. Potassium is 3.3 and creatinine 1.2. During medication review, which option both removes the thiazide exposure associated with potassium loss and provides potassium replacement?

Practice · A 77-year-old man hospitalized for a heart-failure exacerbation becomes confused at night, fails to recognize his wife and tries to leave, although he was alert and oriented that morning. His regular drugs are lisinopril, carvedilol and spironolactone; zolpidem was added three weeks ago. Assessment shows acute onset, inattention and disorganized thinking with normal alertness. Which approach addresses a potentially modifiable contributor?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with newly diagnosed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction feels less breathless after starting low-dose lisinopril. Follow-up shows a small rise in creatinine and potassium, without symptomatic hypotension. The clinician is reviewing whether to continue treatment. Which principle is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, diabetes, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52) reports chronic constipation at her annual visit. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and pravastatin 20 mg daily. Increasing fiber and fluids has not helped. Her daughter reports recent use of ibuprofen 400 mg daily for joint pain. Examination and CBC are normal. Which statement about ibuprofen and constipation follows Hazzard's discussion of NSAIDs?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with hypertension, stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52), and albuminuria is being assessed for antihypertensive treatment. Which statement about treatment selection is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man has frailty with unintentional 15-lb weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, and slow walking speed, and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 36). He takes 12 medications, including atorvastatin 80 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 40 mg. Blood pressure is 108/64 and albumin 3.1. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for reviewing this medication burden?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman living alone has unintentionally lost 8 lb over six months. Her appetite has declined and food no longer tastes the same. She takes lisinopril, metformin, sertraline, and omeprazole; BMI is 20 kg/m2. Which approach incorporates the nutritional screening and medication review described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), heart failure, and mild dementia is hospitalized with volume overload. During intravenous furosemide treatment he develops urinary leakage because he waits too long to reach the toilet. His oral regimen includes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, increased from once daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. Postvoid residual is 30 mL and urinalysis is normal. Which description matches scheduled toileting?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, coronary artery disease, and depression presents with dizziness and weakness. He takes metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, lisinopril, paroxetine 40 mg daily, and recently added amitriptyline 75 mg for neuropathy. BP is 102/68 seated and 84/52 standing, heart rate is 58, and QTc is 492 ms. Which assessment of amitriptyline follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
Practice · A 77-year-old woman takes lithium. An ACE inhibitor or a loop diuretic is being considered. What shared concern does Beers 2023 identify for these combinations?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman presents for Mohs surgery for a 1.2-cm basal cell carcinoma on the tip of her nose. She reports increasing difficulty managing her finances and has missed two appointments. Her daughter confirms that she has recently forgotten to pay bills. Her MMSE score is 22/30. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Which statement about Mohs surgery in older adults is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and knee osteoarthritis is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone and is independent in four of six activities of daily living. Her discharge medications include furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily for knee pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m². If an oral analgesic is still needed after non-drug measures, which initial change best fits the approach on Hazzard p312?

Practice · A 68-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and mild depression reports reduced sexual satisfaction and difficulty with arousal. She takes metformin, lisinopril, and sertraline and feels embarrassed discussing the problem. Which initial communication and assessment approach is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with NYHA class II heart failure, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment wants to begin exercising. He lives alone, has fallen twice in the past year, and takes metformin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. His daughter is concerned about safety. Which approach best applies Hazzard's exercise principles?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has fallen twice in the past month and now needs help with finances and medications. She takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 150/85 supine to 125/75 standing; her get-up-and-go test is abnormal and MMSE is 22/30. Which approach addresses her multiple fall-risk domains?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman has recurrent falls over six months and takes 14 seconds on the Alternate Step Test. She takes lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and recently started solifenacin 5 mg daily. She has difficulty judging curb height despite corrected acuity of 20/25 in each eye. Hazzard recommends a Pelli-Robson chart as part of low-vision assessment. Which visual function does this chart assess?
Practice · Which class of antihypertensive is classically linked to stress incontinence via a chronic cough?
Practice · An older woman takes lithium, and addition of an ACE inhibitor is being considered. Which interaction and recommendation are described in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 85-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia becomes disoriented, pulls at his oxygen cannula, and tries to leave bed after 36 hours without sleep. He is oriented to person only. Home medications are tamsulosin, metformin, and lisinopril. Temperature is 37.8 degrees C, pulse 92, blood pressure 135/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate 22, and oxygen saturation 91% on 2 L/min. His daughter says he would want everything done. Which initial supportive approach accompanies evaluation and treatment of his acute illness?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with coronary disease, previous bypass surgery, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease is euvolemic after treatment of decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He takes carvedilol, lisinopril, and furosemide. Spironolactone is being considered. Which statement follows Hazzard's description of this treatment?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease, MMSE 20, and stage 3 CKD with eGFR 42 repeatedly asks questions and follows his wife around the home. She is exhausted and considering institutional care. He takes memantine 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg; examination and vital signs are unremarkable. Which plan provides caregiver respite and meaningful activity as described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman has had four falls in three months, each while getting up to use the toilet at night. She has poor appetite, temporal wasting, weight 48 kg, BMI 18, grip strength 12 kg, gait speed 0.6 m/s, and albumin 3.0 g/dL. She takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and melatonin 5 mg nightly. Which additional finding is a Fried physical frailty criterion?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with dementia sometimes refuses tablets. After the team adjusts medication administration, she willingly accepts oral treatment. Persistent hypertension requires treatment; a thiazide previously caused hyponatremia, and there is no cardiac indication for a beta-blocker. Renal function and potassium are normal. Which class is the most appropriate initial choice among these options according to Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with heart failure and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) presents after falling while gardening. He reports several days of dizziness and weakness. Medications are furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. Potassium is 5.8 mEq/L, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL (baseline 2.8), and BUN 78. Blood pressure is 102/58 mm Hg and pulse 52. Which change addresses the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist contraindication described in Hazzard?

Practice · אישה בת 73 עם סרטן שד בשלב מוקדם מסרבת לניתוח ואומרת: 'חייתי חיים טובים.' היא עצמאית בכל ה-ADLs, הולכת 2 מיילים ביום, ומתנדבת בכנסייה. התרופה היחידה שלה היא lisinopril 5mg. MMSE 30/30. בתה טוענת שהיא בדיכאון ודורשת הערכה פסיכיאטרית. איזו גישה היא המתאימה ביותר?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with moderate dementia, diabetes, and hypertension is found on the floor, confused and sweating, with glucose 42 mg/dL. He lives alone with weekly family visits. He takes glimepiride 4 mg once daily with breakfast, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily; his recent HbA1c is 6.8%. After treatment with dextrose, which change removes the long-acting sulfonylurea exposure highlighted by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55%), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m2) is reviewed after an exacerbation treated with prednisone 40 mg for 5 days. He remains breathless when dressing and can no longer shop independently. He takes tiotropium, as-needed albuterol, amlodipine 10 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 and room-air oxygen saturation is 93%. Alongside review of his drug treatment, which pulmonary rehabilitation approach is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old man has recovered from pneumonia. Repeated clinic and home blood pressure readings are around 170/90 mm Hg, without orthostatic hypotension. He has untreated stage 2 hypertension and no coronary disease or heart failure. Combination treatment is planned. Which two drug classes should be started at low doses and titrated gradually in this patient?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), atrial fibrillation treated with warfarin, and mild cognitive impairment lives alone. Her daughter reports medication errors, including duplicate doses. She takes warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, and digoxin 0.125 mg daily. INR is 5.8 and digoxin level is 2.4 ng/mL. She is alert but confused about the date. Which intervention best prevents another duplicate dose at home?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with a two-year history of behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia is brought by his daughter for worsening aggression, with compulsive food-taking and inappropriate sexual comments at his nursing facility. Yesterday he pushed another resident who tried to stop him taking dessert. He has hypertension and osteoarthritis, takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and has an MMSE score of 22/30. Which statement about treatment of the compulsive behavior is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has awakened at 3 a.m. nightly for a month. She goes to bed at 9 p.m., falls asleep easily, lies awake from 3 to 5 a.m., and then dozes until 7 a.m. She naps for 30 minutes after lunch. Her medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 500 mg three times daily. Her diary records six hours of sleep and 60% sleep efficiency. Which behavioral intervention follows the sleep-restriction approach?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman in assisted living has moderate macular degeneration with visual acuity 20/200 and heart failure with ejection fraction 35%. She has stopped attending bingo, misses meals, and stays in bed. She takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Potassium is 3.2 and creatinine 1.4, compared with a baseline of 1.0. Alongside assessment of these medical findings, which environmental plan follows Hazzard's low-vision recommendations?

Practice · An 82-year-old man in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a recent left middle cerebral artery stroke with residual hemiparesis develops acute confusion and agitation during dinner. Staff observed food pocketing and failure to swallow before he became aggressive when they tried to help. He has diabetes and hypertension and takes aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, and mirtazapine 15 mg at bedtime. Oxygen saturation falls to 88%, and chest radiography shows a right lower-lobe infiltrate. Which source-described relationship makes a swallowing-related pulmonary complication relevant?
Practice · A patient with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is eligible to switch from an ACE inhibitor to sacubitril/valsartan. Why is a washout period required between the treatments?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with stage 4 CKD, heart failure, and mixed urinary incontinence takes furosemide, carvedilol, and lisinopril. Since starting darifenacin she has had little improvement in urgency and troublesome constipation requiring daily laxatives. Her daughter asks about increasing darifenacin. Which medication-review principle should guide the discussion?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia, diabetes, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m2) has become aggressive, strikes caregivers, and has refused medication for a week. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg. Her daughter requests nursing-home placement for safety. Physical examination shows no evidence of acute illness. Which medication-safety and diagnostic assessment is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45), and chronic insomnia is seen after a fall at home. He has taken zolpidem 10 mg nightly for a year, prescribed by his previous physician. He also takes furosemide, lisinopril, carvedilol, and aspirin. His wife reports morning confusion and two falls in the past month while getting up to use the toilet. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. After medication review, a supervised zolpidem discontinuation plan is made. Which treatment should form the basis of ongoing insomnia care according to Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia, heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and stage 3 CKD has slept more, eaten less, and stopped watching television over two weeks. He takes carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, and citalopram 20 mg daily, started three weeks ago. He has flat affect and psychomotor slowing; sodium is 128, potassium 3.8, and creatinine 1.6. Which approach addresses a recognized medication-related contributor before attributing the change to chronic disease?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presents after a mechanical fall. She takes metformin, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and aspirin. BP is 142/88 and glucose is 52. She reports recurrent dizziness and near-falls. Creatinine is 1.3, eGFR 44, and Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38 mL/min. After treating the hypoglycemia, which assessment of glyburide accords with the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 85-year-old man is found on the kitchen floor after preparing breakfast, with no memory of the collapse. He has Parkinson disease, BPH, hypertension, and chronic back pain. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, tamsulosin 0.8 mg nightly, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and tramadol 50 mg as needed. Examination shows resting tremor and bradykinesia. Which pairing correctly describes two recognized contributors to orthostatic hypotension present in this history?

Practice · An 81-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia is found on the floor and cannot explain what happened. She has osteoporosis, hypertension, and anxiety and takes weekly alendronate, lisinopril 5 mg, and sertraline 50 mg. Her right leg is shortened and externally rotated, and imaging confirms a hip fracture. Hemoglobin is 10.2 and creatinine 1.3. Her son asks how dementia affects the choice of surgery. Which explanation follows Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has three years of worsening word finding and getting lost while driving. Her MMSE is 22/30, with losses in orientation, recall, and naming. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily; eGFR is 52 mL/min. While considering donepezil, the clinician reviews chronic naproxen use. Which statement supports reconsidering naproxen under Beers 2023?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?

Practice · A 78-year-old man has type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45 mL/min). He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg daily, lisinopril 40 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tiotropium, and simvastatin 20 mg daily. He reports two falls on standing in the past month; HbA1c is 7.2%, and blood pressure falls from 128/76 sitting to 108/68 standing. Separate evaluation of the falls is planned. Which medication change best reduces hypoglycemia risk in this patient?

Practice · A 66-year-old woman received high-dose influenza vaccine in October. In March she asks about waning antibodies. She has diabetes and hypertension, takes an ACE inhibitor and a statin, and had no adverse vaccine reaction. Which statement accurately explains the influenza-vaccination recommendation described in Hazzard?

Anticholinergic bladder therapy

passages.section: Cholinesterase Inhibitors, Urinary Incontinence, and Anticholinergic Therapy Initiation
passages.excerpt: Cholinesterase Inhibitors, Urinary Incontinence, and Anticholinergic Therapy Initiation Cholinesterase inhibitors (such as donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine) are often prescribed to manage the symptoms of Alzheimer disease and related dementias.

target.excerpt: Cholinesterase Inhibitors, Urinary Incontinence, and Anticholinergic Therapy Initiation
